title: Open Problem (Section 1): Balanced Separator for $U_t$
statement_text: It is open whether the countable graph $U_t$ constructed by the authors (which contains every $K_t$-minor-free graph as an induced subgraph, has bounded minimum degree on finite subgraphs, bounded $r$-colouring numbers, and no subdivision of $K_{\aleph_0}$) satisfies (K2), that is, whether every finite $n$-vertex subgraph of $U_t$ has a balanced separator of order $O(\sqrt{n})$.
context_text: Graphs in the paper are countable (finite or countably infinite). A graph $U$ contains a class of graphs if every graph of the class is isomorphic to a subgraph of $U$. A separation of a graph $G$ is a pair $(G_1,G_2)$ of subgraphs with $G=G_1\cup G_2$, $E(G_1)\cap E(G_2)=\emptyset$ and both $V(G_1)\setminus V(G_2)$ and $V(G_2)\setminus V(G_1)$ nonempty; its order is $|V(G_1)\cap V(G_2)|$, and it is balanced if $|V(G_i)\setminus V(G_{3-i})|\le\frac23|V(G)|$ for $i=1,2$. For a total order $\preceq$ of $V(G)$, a vertex $w$ is strongly $r$-reachable from $v$ if there is a path $v=w_0,\dots,w_{r'}=w$ of length $r'\le r$ with $w\preceq v$ and $v\prec w_i$ for all internal $w_i$; the $r$-colouring number $\mathrm{col}_r(G)$ is the minimum over orders of the maximum number of vertices strongly $r$-reachable from a vertex. The authors argue that a graph containing every planar graph should share key properties of planar graphs: (K1) every finite subgraph has bounded minimum degree, (K2) every finite $n$-vertex subgraph has a balanced separator of order $O(\sqrt n)$ (as in the Lipton–Tarjan theorem), (K3) bounded $r$-colouring numbers for each $r$, (K4) no subdivision of the countably infinite complete graph $K_{\aleph_0}$. They show that any graph containing all planar graphs has $K_{\aleph_0}$ as a minor and contains subdivisions of every finite $K_t$, and construct graphs such as $\mathcal{T}_6\boxtimes P$ (strong product of a universal treewidth-6 graph with the one-way infinite path) containing all planar graphs and satisfying (K1)–(K3). For each $t\ge3$, using chordal partitions, they construct a graph $U_t$ containing every $K_t$-minor-free graph as an induced subgraph, with no $K_{\aleph_0}$ subdivision, which is $(t-1)(3t-7)$-degenerate and has $\mathrm{col}_r(U_t)\le(t-2)(t-1)(2r+1)$, so it satisfies (K1), (K3), (K4). For $t=5$ this covers planar graphs. Whether $U_t$ also satisfies (K2) is open; a weaker bound of $O(n^{3/4}\log n)$ on balanced separators follows from a result of Plotkin, Rao and Smith.
